football_evidence.question: Can East Carolina win at the line of scrimmage?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.7 points.
supporting: When Memphis has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Memphis’ offense has allowed a sack on 7.3% of its dropbacks, and East Carolina’s defense sacks the quarterback on 10.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Memphis has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Memphis’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 11.7% of its runs, and East Carolina’s defense stops 33.0% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
In his last two games (UAB and Tulane), Stokes averaged 8.1 yards per attempt, against 11.2 in his five games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put East Carolina’s defensive line No. 9 nationally and Memphis’ No. 76.
contradicting: When Memphis has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Memphis’ offense averages 10.2 yards per pass attempt, and East Carolina’s defense allows 7.1 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When Memphis has the ball (big plays through the air): Memphis’ offense turns 14.3% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and East Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 10.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When East Carolina has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): East Carolina’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.9% of its dropbacks, and Memphis’ defense sacks the quarterback on 8.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When East Carolina has the ball (third down): East Carolina’s offense converts 28.4% of its third downs, and Memphis’ defense allows opponents to convert 32.2% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).
quarterbacks: Marcus Stokes has completed 121 of 181 passes (66.9%) for 1,849 yards, 10.2 yards per attempt, 19 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in seven games for Memphis, and has been sacked on 15 of 196 dropbacks.

Emory Williams has completed 67 of 103 passes (65.0%) for 662 yards, 6.4 yards per attempt, 7 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in five games for East Carolina, and has been sacked on 8 of 111 dropbacks.
Mitch Griffis has completed 39 of 71 passes (54.9%) for 422 yards, 5.9 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 1 interception in five games for East Carolina, and has been sacked on 5 of 76 dropbacks.
